record.paper_title: Classification of Finite Groups: Recent Developements and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine all groups of order 1024 up to isomorphism by completing the still-incomplete classification of finite groups of that order. The problem includes both finishing the remaining determination work and, if possible, developing new computational tools that make the required calculations feasible with moderate rather than massive computing power.

evidence.quote: Problem 4 Complete the determination of the groups of order 1024. This problem can perhaps be solved by a straightforward application of the available algorithms using massive computer power. Burrell [ 9] has done a signiﬁcant part of this. It would be interesting to develop new tools that make this computation feasible even with moderate computing power.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $n = 1024 = 2^{10}$. Classify, up to isomorphism, all finite groups of order $n$. That is, produce an explicit list (for example, via presentations or via a small-groups-style library) containing exactly one representative from every isomorphism class of groups of order $1024$, together with a proof that the list is complete and irredundant. A secondary goal is to develop algorithmic tools that make this classification feasible using only moderate computing resources (rather than requiring large-scale computation).
artifact.status_search_result: D. Burrell (Communications in Algebra, 2022) determined the number of groups of order 1024 up to isomorphism to be 49,487,367,289, correcting an earlier count of Eick–O'Brien. However, an explicit, fully implemented classification (e.g., as a SmallGroups library entry in GAP) is not available; only groups of order 1024 of rank at most 4 are accessible through the GRPS1024 GAP package. Thus the enumeration count is settled, but the explicit classification and accompanying lightweight computational tools remain incomplete.

status_evidence.title: On the number of groups of order 1024
status_evidence.snippet: Burrell determines the number of groups of order 1024 up to isomorphism, correcting the earlier Eick–O'Brien count.
status_evidence.claim: The number of groups of order 1024 has been determined (49,487,367,289).

status_evidence.title: Groups of order 1024 - Groupprops
status_evidence.snippet: There are 49,487,367,289 groups of order 1024. GAP's SmallGroup library is not available for this order.
status_evidence.claim: An explicit classification list is not implemented in standard libraries; full classification is not practically available.
